# Entropy Rate and Information in Sequences

Entropy rate generalises Shannon entropy from single variables to stochastic processes. It measures average per-symbol information in the limit of long sequences — directly connecting to language model perplexity and compression limits.

## Definition

$$h = \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{H(X_1,\ldots,X_n)}{n} = \lim_{n\to\infty} H(X_n|X_{n-1},\ldots,X_1)$$

The conditional form is more intuitive: average uncertainty about the next symbol given the entire history. Both limits are equal for stationary processes.

## Entropy Rate of Special Processes

- **i.i.d.:** $h = H(X_1)$
- **Stationary Markov chain:** $h = -\sum_{i,j}\pi_i P_{ij}\log P_{ij}$
- **Gaussian AR(p):** $h = \tfrac{1}{2}\log(2\pi e\,\sigma_\varepsilon^2)$ where $\sigma_\varepsilon^2$ is innovation variance

## Entropy Rate and Language Model Perplexity

$$H_{\text{rate}}(p_{\text{true}}, q_\theta) = -\frac{1}{N}\sum_{t=1}^N \log q_\theta(x_t | x_1,\ldots,x_{t-1}) \xrightarrow{N\to\infty} \text{cross-entropy rate}$$

$$\text{PPL} = \exp(H_{\text{rate}}) \quad \text{(nats)}, \qquad \text{or} \quad 2^{H_{\text{rate}}} \quad \text{(bits)}$$

PPL is the average branching factor — how many equally likely options the model sees at each step.

```python
def compute_perplexity(model, tokenizer, text, stride=512):
    """Stride-based perplexity — avoids boundary effects on long docs."""
    encodings = tokenizer(text, return_tensors='pt')
    input_ids  = encodings.input_ids
    max_len    = model.config.max_position_embeddings
    seq_len    = input_ids.size(1)
    nll_sum, n_tokens, prev_end = 0.0, 0, 0

    for begin_loc in range(0, seq_len, stride):
        end_loc  = min(begin_loc + max_len, seq_len)
        trg_len  = end_loc - prev_end
        chunk    = input_ids[:, begin_loc:end_loc]
        targets  = chunk.clone()
        targets[:, :-trg_len] = -100   # mask context tokens
        with torch.no_grad():
            loss = model(chunk, labels=targets).loss
        nll_sum  += loss.item() * trg_len
        n_tokens += trg_len
        prev_end  = end_loc
        if end_loc == seq_len:
            break

    return float(torch.exp(torch.tensor(nll_sum / n_tokens)))
```

## Empirical Entropy Rate of English

Shannon (1951) estimated ~1.0–1.5 bits/character using human prediction experiments. Modern LLMs achieve ~0.8–1.2 bits/character on well-written text. Zero-order (frequency) model: ~4.0 bits/char; bigram: ~3.5 bits/char; the theoretical max is log₂(27) ≈ 4.75 bits/char.

## Bits-Per-Byte (BPB) as a Tokenizer-Agnostic Metric

$$\text{BPB} = \frac{\log_2(e) \times \text{NLL}_{\text{nats}}}{\text{UTF-8 bytes}}$$

Normalises to the byte level — independent of vocabulary size or tokenisation choices. Standard for comparing models with different tokenizers.

| Metric | Formula | Tokenizer-agnostic | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Perplexity | exp(CE nats) | No | Average branching factor |
| Bits per token | CE bits | No | Avg bits to encode a token |
| Bits per byte (BPB) | CE_bits / bytes_per_token | Yes | Entropy rate in bits/byte |

> **TIP: Perplexity Has a Hard Lower Bound**
> No model can achieve PPL below exp($h_{\text{true}}$). Shannon estimated $h_{\text{true}} \approx 1.0$–$1.3$ bits/char for English — current state-of-the-art LLMs are approaching this limit.

> **WARNING: Naive Perplexity on Long Documents Has Boundary Effects**
> Splitting long docs into fixed chunks ignores cross-chunk context and inflates PPL at boundaries. Stride-based evaluation (overlapping windows, scoring only the final stride tokens) eliminates this at the cost of more computation.
